Filename convention is split: 4 memories use underscores (feedback_premortem_skill_discipline, eci_internal_app, mox_prospect, bastrop_pioneer_narrative) while 100 use hyphens, and wikilinks to them are written with hyphens. Links resolve only under normalization. Per the flag-naming-inconsistencies-early memory, flagging with a recommendation: rename the 4 to hyphens and update the 6 inbound links, OR leave as-is and accept normalization — but do not leave it undecided.

Should a retired-memory marker live in the memory BODY as well as the index? cotality-two-data-paths-map-cache-gap.md is the only file carrying an in-body HISTORICAL marker, and it is the most robust of the five because a reader arriving via a direct [[link]] from a live memory still sees the warning. Recommend making the in-body marker the standard for the superseded-but-linked pattern.
